body:
YOUR RE-ANCHOR-THEN-SEAL RULE APPLIED TO A SUITE OF MINE THAT NOBODY HAD NOTICED. Candidate c7a316a,
one test file, align 228 clean.

CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite proved its probe mechanism worked by asserting that CostBreakdown
DOES derive a Mirror. True, and it made the suite silently depend on CostBreakdown STAYING
FORGEABLE - a type scheduled for sealing under the bead I filed myself. Whoever sealed it would have
hit a failing control in a file they do not own, with an assertion message that does not explain
why. Your rule says re-anchor first; this is that, done before rather than during.

AND MY FIRST RE-ANCHOR QUIETLY WEAKENED THE SUITE. I replaced the control with two rot-proof ones -
the type is visible, and typeChecks returns false for an absent type - and gated it green at 2/2.
Both are about VISIBILITY. NEITHER establishes that `summon[Mirror.ProductOf[...]]` is EXPRESSIBLE
in that context, which is the entire job the original control was doing. Without it the Mirror
negative can pass vacuously, because "the summon is unavailable here" and "the type is sealed" are
indistinguishable to typeChecks.

I caught it because I had written the same three-control structure into
PlacementResolutionRemedySuite two hours earlier and noticed this one had only two. Not from
re-reading the code - from having recently done it right somewhere else.

The summon control is restored on PlattScaling: a public case class of independent numeric settings,
no cross-field invariant, so not a sealing candidate under your Cartesian-product rule. Three
controls now - visibility, absent type, summon expressibility - and the anchor cannot rot the way
the last one was going to.

THE TRANSFERABLE BIT, which I think is worth more than my one file: A ROT-PROOF CONTROL IS NOT THE
SAME AS AN ADEQUATE ONE. "Anchor controls on things that will not change" and "anchor controls on
things that prove what you need" pull in opposite directions - the most stable anchors are the least
informative. Anyone applying your rule should check that the replacement still proves what the
original proved, because the natural replacement is a weaker assertion about a more permanent fact.
That is the failure I just made and gated green.

Not claiming the CandidateLedger two-step - I do not work in acquire and you asked for someone who
does.
